step1_figure.circuit_type: CMOS Differential Amplifier with Current Mirror Load and CMRR Test Circuit
step1_figure.description: The netlist instantiates two identical NMOS diff-pairs with PMOS current-mirror loads and cascode tail current sources biased by SUB_1 (Fig. 20.47 wide-swing cascode bias): one pair configured differentially (VI1 vs VI2) producing Voutd to measure differential gain Ad, and one pair configured in common-mode (both gates driven by VI1) producing Voutc to measure common-mode gain Ac and extract CMRR = Voutd/Voutc as described in Example 22.7.

equation.explanation: Differential voltage gain equals input transistor transconductance multiplied by the parallel output resistance of NMOS M2 and PMOS M4.
equation.assumptions: M1-M4 operating in saturation, symmetric differential pair.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming Iss = 20 uA, Id1 = Id2 = 10 uA. ro2 = 1 / (lambda_n * Id2) = 1 / (0.1 * 10u) = 1 MOhm. ro4 = 1 / (lambda_p * Id4) = 1 / (0.1 * 10u) = 1 MOhm. ro2 || ro4 = 500 kOhm. For (W/L)1,2 = 10/1, beta_n = 270u * 10 = 2.7 mA/V^2. gm1 = sqrt(2 * beta_n * Id1) = sqrt(2 * 2.7m * 10u) = 232 uS. Ad = 232 uS * 500 kOhm = 116 V/V = 41.3 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard single-stage current-mirror load diff-amp gain is gm * ro / 2, typically 30 to 45 dB in standard submicron CMOS.

equation.explanation: Common-mode gain is inversely proportional to twice the product of mirror load transconductance and tail current source output resistance Ro.
equation.assumptions: M3 and M4 matched, tail current source has output resistance Ro.

sky130_expected.calculation: For PMOS mirror (W/L)=20/1, beta_p = 50u * 20 = 1.0 mA/V^2. gm3,4 = sqrt(2 * 1.0m * 10u) = 141 uS. For a cascode current source, Ro ≈ gm_cas * ro^2 ≈ 200 uS * (1 MOhm)^2 = 200 MOhm. Ac = 1 / (2 * 141 uS * 200 MOhm) = 1.77e-5 V/V = -95 dB. In real layout/channel-length effects, Ro is 10M to 50M Ohm, giving Ac ≈ -70 dB to -85 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: High output resistance from cascode tail current source significantly attenuates common-mode variations.

common_mode_rejection_ratio.description: Ratio of differential gain to common-mode gain

equation.formula: CMRR = 20 * log10(|Ad / Ac|) = 20 * log10(gm1,2 * (ro2 || ro4) * 2 * gm3,4 * Ro)
equation.explanation: Measures the amplifier's ability to reject input signals common to both inputs.
equation.assumptions: Both differential and common-mode stages operate in saturation with identical biasing.

sky130_expected.calculation: CMRR(dB) = Ad(dB) - Ac(dB) = 41.3 dB - (-75 dB) = 116.3 dB with cascode tail source, or ~86 dB as calculated in textbook text for standard cascode tail.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Textbook Example 22.7 reports 86 dB low-frequency CMRR with cascode tail; with 700 mV common-mode bias, simulation achieves 80-90 dB.

vcm_max.description: Maximum allowable common-mode input voltage to keep input pair in saturation

equation.explanation: Input voltage where input NMOS drain-to-gate junction enters triode boundary.
equation.assumptions: Drain of M1 is held at VDD - VSG3 by diode-connected PMOS load.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Input can swing above VDD - VSG by up to one NMOS threshold voltage before M1/M2 enter triode.

vcm_min.description: Minimum allowable common-mode input voltage to keep tail current source in saturation

equation.explanation: Sum of gate-to-source voltage of input pair and saturation compliance voltage of cascode tail current source.
equation.assumptions: Cascode tail source requires 2 * VDS,sat to remain in saturation.

sky130_expected.calculation: VGS1,2 = VTHN + Vov,n = 0.42 + 0.086 ≈ 0.51 V. Cascode tail drop = 2 * VDS,sat ≈ 2 * 0.1 V = 0.2 V. VCMMIN = 0.51 + 0.20 = 0.71 V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: At least two overdrive voltages plus VGS are needed to maintain saturation across the tail cascode stack.

equation.explanation: Determined by keeping PMOS M4 in the saturation region.
equation.assumptions: M4 remains saturated as output swings up toward VDD.

sky130_expected.calculation: VDD = 1.8 V. VSD,sat4 ≈ 0.14 V. VOUTMAX = 1.8 - 0.14 = 1.66 V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Limited by one PMOS saturation overdrive voltage below VDD.

equation.explanation: Determined by the gate voltage on M2 keeping M2 in saturation.
equation.assumptions: M2 gate is biased at VI2 = 0.7 V.

sky130_expected.calculation: VI2 = 0.70 V. With body effect VTHN ≈ 0.50 V to 0.60 V (or nominal 0.42 V). VOUTMIN = 0.70 - 0.42 = 0.28 V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: M2 remains saturated as long as Vdrain >= Vgate - Vthn.

differential_input_range.description: Maximum differential input range before one input transistor cuts off

equation.explanation: Differential input voltage at which all tail current is steered through one transistor.
equation.assumptions: Square-law saturation model for input NMOS pair.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Equal to sqrt(2) * Vov of the input pair at balanced operating point.

3db_frequency.description: Output -3 dB corner frequency when driving a 1 pF load capacitance

equation.explanation: Dominated by output high-impedance pole formed by ro2 || ro4 and load capacitance CL.
equation.assumptions: Output node is the dominant high-impedance pole; CL = 1 pF.

sky130_expected.calculation: ro2 || ro4 ≈ 500 kOhm. CL = 1 pF. f3dB = 1 / (2 * pi * 500 kOhm * 1 pF) ≈ 318 kHz. With lower ro || ro ≈ 111 kOhm (as in textbook 0.5um process), f3dB = 1.4 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined directly by output RC time constant with 1 pF load.

step3_testbench.description: Comprehensive ngspice testbench for Baker Ch 22 Diff-Amp CMRR circuit: executes AC analysis to measure differential gain (Ad), common-mode gain (Ac), CMRR (Voutd/Voutc), and -3dB bandwidth, followed by DC operating point and DC common-mode input sweep to measure VCM limits and output swing.
